suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-15 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. A nationally representative survey found eating disorders, including binge eating disorder, significantly comorbid with many other DSM-IV disorders; the approved relationship is limited to population-level comorbidity association and does not establish direction of onset or individual causation. Require independently established binge eating disorder and separately established depressive disorder; the cited nationally representative survey found eating disorders significantly comorbid with many other DSM-IV disorders without establishing direction of onset. Preserve obesity and metabolic disease, other eating pathology, substance use, medications, and other psychiatric illness as competing explanations. Do not infer a depressive disorder from binge eating symptoms, weight change, or role impairment alone, and do not treat this population-level association as proof that binge eating disorder caused an individual's depressive disorder. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
